simple: A preset system lets players send ready-made messages, like "Need help" or "Reloading", often by picking from a wheel. Because anyone can use them, even players who cannot free-chat, Roblox has strict rules: presets must be about gameplay, not conversation. This page explains what phrases are allowed, what is banned, and the technical requirements like filtering and rate limits. If you want this feature, Roblox's built-in Quick Words already follows all the rules.
analogy: It is like hand signals in a sports team: "pass", "cover me", "ready". They help the team play, but you could never use them to have a real conversation about your weekend.
keyPoints: Presets are for quick gameplay coordination, not for chatting. They must not let players of different ages have free, two-way conversations or get around safety systems.
Each preset must stand alone, fit the current game moment, and avoid open-ended or social language. Simple call and reply like "Help" then "OK" is fine.
Good examples: "Need help", "Defending this area", "Ready", "Pass the ball", "Reloading", "Enemy nearby".
Bad examples: "Why didn't you help me?", "Do you like me?", "Where are you from?", "What are your socials?", greetings like "Hi!" and "How are you?".
No alphabet wheels, number codes, or combos that let players spell out any message.

Requirements: label presets as system preset in chat, make them look different from normal chat, use no end punctuation (no ! ? or .), filter them with `TextService:FilterStringAsync()`, rate-limit to one send per 10 seconds, and show 12 presets or fewer.
Roblox may review your preset system and require changes, disable it, or take action on your game, account, or group if it breaks the rules.
Roblox's built-in Quick Words already follows these guidelines, so you can use it instead of building your own.

terms.preset: A message written ahead of time by the game creator that players can pick and send, like "Ready".
terms.preset system: The feature, like a wheel or menu, that lets players send presets.
terms.two-way communication: A real back-and-forth conversation between players.
terms.circumvent: To get around a rule or safety system on purpose.
terms.age check: Roblox confirming a player's age, through Facial Age Estimation or ID verification.
terms.terminal punctuation: Marks that end a sentence: period, question mark, exclamation mark. Presets must not use them.
terms.rate limit: A cooldown on how often something can be sent. Here, one preset per 10 seconds.
terms.encode: Hide a message in a code, like using numbers to stand for letters. Not allowed in presets.
terms.slang: Casual words whose meaning can change or be hidden. Presets must avoid it.
terms.Universe: Your whole game, including all of its places.

watchOut: Writing presets as questions or greetings. Keep them to short gameplay actions like "Attack" or "Follow me".
Adding punctuation like "Ready!". Leave off end marks so presets do not look like normal chat.
Offering more than 12 presets, or letting players spam them. Cap at 12 and add a 10-second cooldown.
Skipping filtering because you wrote the text yourself. Presets still must go through `TextService:FilterStringAsync()`.
Making presets look exactly like regular chat. Label them as system preset and style them differently.
Building your own when Quick Words would do. Quick Words already follows these rules.
